summary: The research holds up well. Every revenue rate in the financial model matches its primary source: CareScout FL non-medical caregiver $32/hr (rank 39, $73,216 at 44 h/wk, +7%), Medicaid FFS S9122 $17.32/hr, APD S5130UC agency $6.07/QH with 7/1/2024 still the latest APD change, and Pasco-Pinellas AAA $27.00-$29.92 / $26.00-$27.30. Every wage matches BLS OEWS 2025 via O*NET; the hourly figures are the annual figures divided by 2080: aides FL 25th/median/75th $15.16/$16.25/$17.25, Tampa median $16.45 and 75th $17.42, Miami $15.81, Orlando $16.40; RN FL $40.48, Tampa $41.09; Tampa social and community service manager 25th $62,020 and median $77,560; Tampa first-line supervisor of personal service workers $46,250; Tampa medical secretary $43,770 ($21.04/hr). All wages are at or above the $15.00 Florida minimum effective 9/30/2026 (Fla. Const. Art. X s.24), and s.218.077 preempts local minimum wages. Fees check out: HHA $1,705 + $300 assessment (checklist 3110-1011CL), homemaker/companion registration $50.75 + $25 amended certificate, nurse registry $2,000, LLC $100 + $25, LLC annual report $138.75 with a $400 late fee, IRS mileage 72.5 cents. The statutory requirements also check out: $250,000/claim malpractice and liability insurance; CPA-compiled 2-year projections with no month in year 1 at a 15%+ margin; 3 months of average projected expenses with contingency of at least 1 month; non-skilled agencies exempt from accreditation; DON required only for skilled care; RN supervisory visits as needed, with patient consent and agreement to pay; 36.9-month survey cycle; 8 consecutive hours of availability; 40-hour aide training or the 14-task / 90-of-104 competency test; dementia training under s.430.5025, which covers companion/homemaker staff because its definition of personal care includes companion services; nurse registry contractor rules; planning-district service areas for registrants. Contacts verified: (850) 412-4500, 850-412-4503, 1-877-711-3662, 1-800-962-2873. Enrollment and demand figures verified against ENR_202609.xls (176,819 / 125,912 / 50,907; 174,349 the prior month; Dade 61,139, Broward 13,647, Hillsborough 12,746, Palm Beach 11,755, Pinellas 8,844), the APD Q4 FY25-26 report (37,645; 15,504; 9,750; 61.5-61.7% not receiving services) and Census QuickFacts (23,462,518; 22.8%; 8.9%). Recomputing the model reproduces every figure in the narrative: default net, margin, conservative net, break-even occupancy, every sensitivity, the $23.20 and $26.12 LTC break-even rates, $28.88 / $29.69 break-even private prices, the APD 60-client result of +$3,672, first profitable month 10, the $80,219 deficit and the required reserves. No critical issues. The one major issue: S9122 is Florida Medicaid's state-plan personal care benefit for recipients under 21, so it is described wrongly as the adult LTC benchmark. The minor issues are citation and label fixes.

issues.current: S9122 $17.32/hr presented as 'Florida Medicaid's only published hourly personal care rate' and used as the benchmark for SMMC LTC plan rates, with no note of who the benefit covers
issues.correct: The $17.32 rate is correct, but S9122 is the Medicaid state-plan Personal Care Services benefit, which covers recipients under age 21 (EPSDT). It is not an adult LTC rate, and SMMC LTC plan rates for adults are negotiated separately.
issues.evidence: Rule 59G-4.215 Personal Care Services Coverage Policy: 'Florida Medicaid recipients under the age of 21 years requiring medically necessary personal care...'. The 2026 Personal Care Services Fee Schedule lists S9122 at $17.32/hr.
issues.fix: Keep $17.32 as a labeled assumption. Wherever it appears, add: 'S9122 is the fee-for-service state-plan personal care rate for Medicaid recipients under 21 (Rule 59G-4.215); adult LTC plan rates are negotiated, are not published, and may be higher or lower.' Add the coverage policy as a new source. The break-even rate ($23.20/hr at minimum wage) stays as stated.

issues.evidence: In Rule 59A-8.0095, subsection (3) 'Registered Nurse', paragraphs (c)-(d), holds the RN supervisory-visit, written-consent and 'on-site supervision as needed' text. Subsection (5) covers home health aides.
issues.fix: Replace 'Rule 59A-8.0095(5)' with 'Rule 59A-8.0095(3)(c)-(d)' in all four places.
